_comment: SCHEMA EXAMPLE ONLY, with made-up product ids 900/901. The real, verified Basilisk V3 rule set is rules.json.
Routes are tried in order; the first whose 'backend' matches the active backend and whose 'match' regex matches the request path (no query string) wins.

route fields: name, backend (string | array | omitted = all backends), match (regex), host (upstream host, default upstreamHost), path (String.replace template applied to the request path, default = same path), pathRewrite (list of rewrite entries applied to the mapped upstream path), keepQuery (default true), noStore (default true: Cache-Control no-store + no ETag), textTypes (regex on Content-Type, default js/html/json/css/plain; octet-stream falls back to file extension), noRewrite (regex on the request path: body rewrites skipped, body served byte-identical), rewrite (list).

rewrite entries: {literal, replace} or {pattern, flags (default g), replace} with String.replace semantics ($1, $<name>, $&). Optional: name (for logs), paths (regex on the request path that limits the entry), expect ({"<upstream path suffix>": count}; another count is logged as warn= and listed by /__mirror/status), required (regex on the request path; a 2xx response there with 0 matches is refused with 502 instead of being served unpatched). Rewrites only run on 2xx textual bodies.
jsonEdits fields: name, match, backend, key (default productId), ensure / remove (array roots), set / setIfMissing (object roots, dotted paths).
resolve (optional): {"apps-mac.razer.com": ["<real ip>"]} pins the upstream IP instead of DNS; loopback is always refused.
